LABORATORY REPORT
Patient: Age 71, Sex Male
Clinical context: History of bladder cancer; surveillance cystoscopy equivocal.
Analyte | Result | Unit | Reference
Urine FISH (chromosomes 3, 7, 17 and 9p21) | Positive (polysomy in 12% of cells) |  | Negative
Urine cytology | Atypical urothelial cells |  | Negative
closed_direct.prompt:
Question: What is the most appropriate interpretation? Choose ONE option (A–D) and give a one-sentence justification.
A. Positive FISH with atypical cytology indicates likely recurrence; biopsy of suspicious area and/or enhanced cystoscopy
B. Negative surveillance; continue routine follow-up
C. Findings indicate benign inflammation
D. Result cannot be interpreted
